2026-09-22 JUDGMENT, standard = gpt-5.6-sol: OpenAI's GPT-6 line ships three classes where this map has four. Rather than list gpt-6-sol at two tiers or invent an id, standard keeps gpt-5.6-sol, which is still selectable on the hosts this catalog targets (it appears, and is the active selection, in the Cursor model picker) even though it has left OpenAI's current API model list alongside gpt-5.6-terra and gpt-5.6-luna. This is the cell to re-check FIRST on the next refresh: a model a picker still offers but the vendor's current list omits is the one most likely to retire next. If it retires, collapse the tier onto gpt-6-sol at medium effort.

2026-09-22 JUDGMENT, OpenAI tier order: the API docs call GPT-6 Astra (gpt-6-astra) 'our most capable model' ($10/$50), gpt-6-sol a performance/cost balance ($2/$10), and gpt-6-luna 'our most efficient model' ($0.1/$0.5). Astra shipped three weeks before the other two as the flagship and sits one class ABOVE Sol; it does NOT replace gpt-5.6-terra. The model picker lists Sol before Astra, so picker order is not capability order. The 'Astra-level reliability at much lower cost' claim concerns reliability measured against GPT-5.6 Sol, not capability parity with Astra.
